inputs.name: location
inputs.label: Hetzner location
inputs.description: The Hetzner location the host runs in, fsn1, nbg1 or hel1. These are Hetzner's locations in the EU, so the app's data stays there, and they share one network zone, so servers in different locations can sync data over a private network. The server, its primary IP and its volume all live in this one location, which cannot change once they stand. Left empty, they live in nbg1.

inputs.name: serverType
inputs.label: Server type
inputs.description: The Hetzner server types, in the order the block tries them, such as cx23 alone, or cx23 then cpx22. Each type's vCPUs are shared: cx23 and cpx22 have 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of memory, cx33 and cpx32 have 4 vCPUs and 8 GB, and cx43 and cpx42 have 8 vCPUs and 16 GB. cpx52 has 12 vCPUs and 24 GB, and cx53 and cpx62 have 16 vCPUs and 32 GB. A cpx type has twice the disk of the cx type with as many vCPUs. The server is created as the first type of the list that Hetzner can order in its location, so a later type stands in when an earlier one is sold out. It has no default, because blocks that create a server want different sizes, and each block refuses a type it does not run on or a list longer than it takes. A server keeps the type it was created with, so an upgrade may add types to the list but never drop one.

manyInputs.name: cloudPoolServerTypes
manyInputs.label: Cloud pool server types
manyInputs.description: The Hetzner server types of the Cloud pool's workers, in the order the block tries them, such as cpx32 alone or cpx32,cx43. A worker is created as the first type of the list that Hetzner can order in its location.

manyInputs.name: cloudPoolLocations
manyInputs.label: Cloud pool locations
manyInputs.description: The Hetzner locations the Cloud pool's workers spread over, such as fsn1,nbg1. A new worker takes the listed location that holds the fewest workers.

manyInputs.name: cloudPoolMin
manyInputs.label: Cloud pool minimum
manyInputs.description: The fewest Cloud workers the pool keeps. A minimum equal to the maximum keeps that many workers. A lower minimum lets the pool add a worker for each pod that waits for room, and remove a worker that stood idle for cloudPoolIdleMinutes, between the two bounds.

manyInputs.name: cloudPoolMax
manyInputs.label: Cloud pool maximum
manyInputs.description: The most Cloud workers the pool keeps, which caps what its burst can cost. A maximum equal to the minimum keeps that many workers.

manyInputs.name: cloudPoolIdleMinutes
manyInputs.label: Cloud pool idle minutes
manyInputs.description: How many minutes a Cloud worker of a pool whose minimum is below its maximum may run no pod but the cluster's own before the pool drains and deletes it, from 1 to 120. Such a pool needs it, and a pool of a set size ignores it. The window stops at 120 minutes so it fits inside the node reports mitstack keeps of the cluster.
